draft.title: Buddhist sexual ethics
card: The third of the five precepts is a training rule to avoid sexual misconduct. Buddhists take it on as a commitment to live well, not as a command from a god.
The precept is usually understood in terms of harm. Sexual conduct that hurts others through betrayal, deceit, force or lack of consent is seen as misconduct.
Traditions and teachers apply the precept differently. Some give detailed guidance, and others leave more to the judgement of each person.
Buddhists often link the precept to ideas such as compassion, honesty and intention. Craving and clinging can lead to suffering for oneself and others, so the aim is to act with care.
draft.remember: The third precept is a training rule that asks Buddhists to avoid harm in relationships, and teachers apply it in different ways.

a.q: Why do many Buddhists see betraying a partner's trust as sexual misconduct?
opts: It causes harm to others through deceit
It breaks a commandment given by a god
It is banned in every Buddhist school equally
It shows a person has not become a monk or nun
a.why: The third precept is usually understood in terms of avoiding harm, and betrayal and deceit hurt others. It is a training rule that Buddhists take on, not a command from a god, and schools do not all apply it in the same way.
a.clue: Think about what the precept asks Buddhists to avoid causing.

b.q: Two Buddhist teachers give different advice on a question about relationships, yet both say they follow the third precept. What best explains this?
opts: Teachers and schools apply the precept in different ways
One of the teachers has rejected the precept
The precept has no link to harm in relationships
Only the older teacher can interpret the precept
b.why: The precept is a training rule, and teachers and schools apply it differently while both aim to avoid harm. Neither teacher needs to have rejected it, and the precept is closely linked to avoiding harm, so the third option is wrong.
b.clue: Consider whether one shared precept can be applied in more than one way.

a.best: It causes harm to others through deceit

b.best: Teachers and schools apply the precept in different ways
